title: Stable exits never listed → agent re-tries only known edges (missing-exit extraction)
root_cause_hypothesis: The LLM extraction under-reports the stable's exits (only 'down'/'out' ever get wired as edges), so update_graph never creates Unknown placeholders for north/south/west/in — the unknown-exit scanner in determine_next_action can only pick directions that were extracted, and no guard forces cardinal-direction coverage; the anomaly originates in llm.extract_knowledge's exit list, not decision_logic.
change_summary: The agent only ever explores exits that were extracted into the graph as Unknown placeholders; since the LLM keeps dropping the stable's cardinal exits (north/south/west) and 'in', those directions never become candidate edges and determine_next_action re-cycles the only two it knows ('down'/'out'). Fix the origin layer by strengthening extract_knowledge's exit parsing/few-shot examples so exit lists like the stable's are captured completely (add a few-shot example for a room whose 'Exits' line lists multiple cardinal directions plus in/out, and tighten the extraction prompt to enumerate every direction word literally present). This is deliberately kept off the hot path — no new LLM calls are added, only the existing extraction is made more accurate. Do NOT mark 'down'/'out' futile: the steps are non-productive but the correct remedy is capturing the missing exits, not giving up on directions.
acceptance_criteria: In a future run log, after re-entering 'dingy stable' the world_graph shows Unknown-exit edges (or resolved edges) for north/south/west and 'in', not only down/out.
The step 16-24 sequence no longer repeats 'down'/'out' 7 times; the log shows at least one attempt of a cardinal direction or 'in' from the stable within the window following re-entry.

extract_knowledge returns the full exit list for a stable-style response containing multiple cardinal directions plus in/out (verifiable against the raw response text in the run log's 'extracted.exits').
